title: Atrium 0.25.6
notes:
This update adds automatic idle session title refreshing using the configured memory model, along with a synced General Settings toggle and multi-turn title prompts.

## Added

- **Automatic idle title refresh (`Session`, `SessionStore`)**: Automatically refreshes unlocked task titles 3 seconds after a completed turn (`finishTurn(.endTurn)`) returns to `.idle` with no queued messages, pending permissions, or elicitations. Auto-refreshed titles stay unlocked so subsequent turns can refine the title while suppressing late agent-proposed `session_info_update` titles for the same turn; manually renamed, manually refreshed, or chief-assigned (`setInitialTitle`) titles remain locked, and demo/subagent/restored/cancelled/failed/usage-limited turns are skipped silently without showing a header spinner or error notice.
- **Auto-refresh title setting & daemon sync (`GeneralPage`, `DaemonServer`, `DaemonProtocol`, `DaemonChange`)**: Added an **Auto-refresh title** toggle (`autoRefreshTitleOnIdle`, enabled by default) in **Settings › General** with Simplified Chinese localization, persisted in daemon `UserDefaults`, synced across `DaemonSnapshot` / `DaemonChange` (including the web client sync layer), and updated via the `settings/set_auto_refresh_title` RPC (allowed for local and remote Mac app connections, refused for browser remote, MCP, and automation connections).

## Changed

- **Multi-turn title refresh prompt (`SessionTitle.refreshPrompt`)**: Includes the latest distinct user message alongside the first user message and latest assistant reply (each bounded to `excerptLength`) so later-turn refreshes reflect how the conversation evolved.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.5
notes:
This update adds end-to-end Kitty Graphics Protocol support and comprehensive terminal image pasting, supporting both Kitty clipboard/paste events (`OSC 5522` / `DEC mode 5522`) and standard macOS paste and drag-and-drop workflows.

## Added

- **Kitty Graphics Protocol (`TerminalHost`, `TerminalRelay`, `TerminalReplay`, `TerminalFrame`)**: Propagates PTY pixel dimensions (`ws_xpixel`, `ws_ypixel`) across `terminal/create`, `terminal/attach`, `TerminalSavedRecord`, `TerminalPTY`, and 4- or 8-byte binary resize frames (`pixelSize` handshake negotiation for backwards compatibility), configures an explicit 320 MB `image-storage-limit` in `GhosttyConfiguration`, and filters replayed `APC G` streams so queries (`a=q`, including continuations) are stripped while image uploads retain only `q=2` on opening chunks.
- **Kitty Clipboard Protocol & Paste Events (`OSC 5522`, `DEC mode 5522`, `GhosttyRuntime`, `TerminalSurfaceView`)**: Supports `CSI ? 5522 h` paste event notifications and `pw`-authenticated follow-up reads via a 15-second snapshotted `pasteGrant` (`TerminalPasteSnapshot`) with lazy ImageIO PNG transcoding and multi-MIME clipboard writes (`TerminalClipboard.write`).
- **Standard Image Paste & Drag-and-Drop (`TerminalClipboard`, `TerminalSurfaceView`)**: Handles `⌘V`, **Edit › Paste** / **Paste and Match Style**, context-menu **Paste**, `NSMenuItemValidation`, and Finder/image drag-and-drop—saving raw PNG/TIFF clipboard images to private temporary `.png` files (`0700`/`0600`, auto-pruned) and pasting shell-escaped paths, prioritizing Finder `file://` URLs over bare filename/icon types and disabling local temp-file fallback on remote terminals (`opensFileLinks == false`).

## Changed

- **Clipboard Security & Paste Flow Control (`GhosttyConfiguration`, `TerminalClipboardPolicy`, `TerminalHost`)**: Enables `clipboard-read = ask` so Ghostty's `pw`-authenticated `OSC 5522` paste grants work while ungranted `OSC 52` / `OSC 5522` reads route to `confirm_read_clipboard_cb` and are unconditionally denied, and adds `TerminalConnection` `DispatchSourceRead` backpressure (`1 MiB` pause / `512 KiB` resume / `4 MiB` hard limit) so large base64 image pastes stream cleanly without disconnecting.

## Fixed

- **Direct Tunnel Socket Fallback (`DirectTunnel`)**: Reserved 16 hex characters (matching `UInt64` FNV-1a tags) when checking the 104-byte Unix socket path limit before falling back to `/tmp`.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.4
notes:
This update relaxes remote access network restrictions so any reachable IPv4/IPv6 network address or reverse proxy can connect while keeping TLS 1.3, password/lockout, certificate pinning, and CSRF protections intact, and drops the legacy network scope model.

## Changed

- **Wildcard dual-stack binding (`RemoteHostBinding`, `RemoteServer`, `BonjourRecordCodec`)**: Remote access now listens on `0.0.0.0` and `::` (with `IPV6_V6ONLY` when IPv4 is also bound, graceful fallback on IPv4-only systems, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 client address normalization) instead of restricting listeners to per-scope addresses; isolated test-harness runs remain on `127.0.0.1`. Bonjour continues advertising on the local network when binding wildcard addresses.
- **Reachable address display (`RemoteHostBinding`, `RemoteAddressFormat`, `RemotePage`)**: `remote/status` lists all reachable non-loopback IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (Tailscale IPv4/IPv6, private LAN IPv4, public/other routable IPv4 & IPv6) plus `127.0.0.1`, filtering out unspecified, APIPA, proxy fake-IP TUN (`198.18.0.0/15`), multicast, reserved, and link-local IPv6 addresses. **Settings › Remote** labels Tailscale, Local Network, and Localhost (`本机`) addresses, truncates long IPv6 endpoints in the middle, and updates the subtitle in English and Simplified Chinese.
- **Reverse-proxy & cross-site navigation support (`RemoteOriginCheck`, `DirectTunnel`)**: Safe static `GET`/`HEAD` requests to Atrium Web are allowed across `Sec-Fetch-Site` while `POST` mutations and WebSocket upgrades continue enforcing same-origin checks. `Origin` validation normalizes case and default ports (`:443`/`:80`) and matches against `Host`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Port`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and RFC 7239 `Forwarded`. Direct Mac connections now send TLS SNI (for DNS hostnames) and the actual target `Host` header so domain-based reverse proxies work out of the box.

## Removed

- **Legacy network scopes (`RemoteScope`, `scopes`)**: Removed `RemoteScope`, the `scopes` field/parameter from `RemoteConfig`, `RemoteAccessStatus`, `remote/set_config`, and `SessionStore.setRemoteAccess`, and the **Scope** checkboxes from **Settings › Remote › Advanced…** (existing `config.json` files continue decoding cleanly while ignoring legacy keys).

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.3
notes:
This update reworks window background transparency and background blur after iTerm2's AppKit and CoreGraphics implementation.

## Changed

- **Pure alpha window backdrop (`WindowBackdropView`, `WindowChrome`)**: Replaced behind-window `NSVisualEffectView` material with a single non-animated alpha canvas layer over a `0.01`-alpha near-clear window backing color (`WindowChrome.translucentWindowBackgroundColor`) with explicit shadow invalidation on opaque transitions and automatic solid-canvas fallback in native full screen.
- **WindowServer Gaussian blur (`WindowBackgroundBlur`)**: Dynamically resolves `CGSDefaultConnectionForThread` / `CGSMainConnectionID` and `CGSSetWindowBackgroundBlurRadius` from `ApplicationServices.framework`, applies iTerm2's per-window `_minBlur` workaround so toggling blur off and back on never breaks WindowServer blur, and re-synchronizes blur across window presentation, key activation, deminiaturization, and full-screen transitions in both main and auxiliary windows.
- **Full `0%–100%` translucency & sticky bar clipping**: Removed the previous `15%` / `35%` material opacity floors across `WindowTranslucencyPreferences` and `TranslucencyScale`, and clipped scrolled conversation rows behind the pinned sticky tool bar (`TopEdgeFade.coveredTop`) without a separate behind-window material view.

## Added

- **Background blur and blur radius settings (`GeneralPage`)**: Added a **Background blur** toggle (`translucentWindowBlur`, enabled by default) and a **Blur radius** slider (`1–64`, `translucentWindowBlurRadius`, default `20`) in **Settings › General**, with automatic enablement gating (blur toggle disabled at `0%` translucency; blur radius slider disabled at `0%` or when blur is off), Simplified Chinese localization, and KVO synchronization in Ghostty and embedded Neovim views.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.2
notes:
This update fixes spacing and alignment inside the top-bar workspace switcher.

## Fixed

- **Workspace tab spacing (`ToolbarViewTabsView`)**: Replaced default `NSButton` image/title layout with a dedicated `ToolbarTabButton` layout that enforces uniform outer (`2 pt`), inter-segment (`2 pt`), horizontal (`10 pt`), icon-to-title (`5 pt`), title-to-dot (`6 pt`), and dot-to-count (`4 pt`) spacing with symmetric padding across Tasks, Terminal, and Browser tabs in both English and Simplified Chinese.
- **Stable widths & alignment**: Accounted for `NSTextField` alignment rect insets and SF Symbol full image sizes, and reserved medium-weight title width so switching between workspaces no longer shifts adjacent tabs.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.1
notes:
This update adds direct keyboard shortcuts for switching top-level workspaces and selecting Terminal and Browser tabs.

## Added

- **Workspace switching with `⌥1` / `⌥2` / `⌥3`**: Switch between **Tasks** (`⌥1`), **Terminal** (`⌥2`), and **Browser** (`⌥3`) from any window (main window, Scratch Terminal, and Software Update) and any focused input surface (composer, Ghostty terminal, `WKWebView`, or embedded Neovim), without leaking Option characters or Meta escape sequences, while yielding when a modal dialog or Settings layer is open.
- **Terminal and Browser tab switching with `⌘1`–`⌘9`**: Added `Terminal › Switch Tab` (`Tab 1`–`Tab 8` and `Last Tab` on `⌘9`) and view-level `⌘1`–`⌘9` handling in `TerminalDrawerView` and `BrowserWorkspaceView`. Standalone terminals (global Terminal workspace and Scratch Terminal) always respond to `⌘1`–`⌘9`, while the per-task terminal drawer intercepts them only when focus is inside the drawer so `⌘1` continues toggling the timeline in conversation and editor views.
- **Toolbar hints & localization**: Updated the workspace tab tooltips (`Tasks (⌥1)`, `Terminal (⌥2)`, `Browser (⌥3)`) with Simplified Chinese translations and automatically focus the global terminal when switching to it via `⌥2`.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.25.0
notes:
This update adds production MCP, Skills, and `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` support across Atrium and its built-in agent, and changes new sessions to use the chosen folder directly without creating a Git worktree by default.

## Added

- **MCP server management and runtime support**:
  - Added `MCPStore` and `MCPServerConfig` in `AtriumCore` supporting native arrays, Claude Desktop / Cursor `{"mcpServers": {...}}` and `{"servers": {...}}` objects, stdio (`command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`) and remote HTTP/SSE (`url`, `headers`) transports, workspace `.mcp.json` and `.atrium/mcp.json` merging with sandbox fence checks, reserved server filtering (`atrium`, `atrium_screen`), and `0600` atomic saves in `~/.config/atrium/mcp.json`.
  - Built `MCPHub`, `MCPStdioClient`, and `MCPHTTPClient` in `AtriumAgent` with concurrent session startup, per-server timeouts and failure isolation, JSON-RPC 2.0 cursor-paginated `tools/list` and `resources/list`, cancellation notifications, Streamable HTTP + `text/event-stream` SSE parsing, `Mcp-Session-Id` propagation, collision-safe tool name prefixing, read-only hint classification for `explore` subagents, `mcp_resources_list` / `mcp_resource_read` resource helpers, and connection probing.
  - Forwarded configured enabled MCP servers into compatible external ACP agent sessions via `Session.openingMCPServers()`, and redacted MCP credentials and sensitive headers across `Session` ACP traces and `AgentSession` histories and tool outputs.
  - Added AppKit MCP management UI in **Settings › Agent** (`MCPEditorCard`, `MCPRowView`) with Stdio/HTTP configuration, inline enable/disable and removal, and live **Test Connection** probing.
- **Skills discovery and invocation**:
  - Added `SkillCatalog` in `AtriumCore` to discover `SKILL.md` skills and Markdown commands across workspace (`.atrium/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.claude/commands`) and user (`~/.config/atrium/skills`, `~/.atrium/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`) locations with case-insensitive workspace precedence and SandboxFence credential protection.
  - Integrated skills into the built-in `atrium` agent: system prompt `Available skills` summary, built-in `skill` tool (available in both normal and `explore` subagent modes), ACP `.availableCommands` advertisement, and `/<skill>` slash command autocompletion and inline skill expansion.
  - Added **Skills & Instructions** status and quick shortcuts (`Open Skills Folder`, `Edit Global AGENTS.md`) to **Settings › Agent**.
- **`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` instructions**:
  - Updated `SystemPrompt` to load global (`~/.config/atrium/` and fallbacks) and Git-root-to-working-directory instruction hierarchies (`AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.atrium/AGENTS.md`, and `*.local.md`), expand `@path` / `@"path"` imports outside code fences and inline code with cycle/size/fence guards, and lazily attach unseen subdirectory `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` rules when reading, searching, or editing files inside nested folders.

## Changed

- **New sessions default to no Git worktree**: Updated `NewTaskCard` so `New worktree` starts unchecked, opening new tasks directly in the selected folder unless a separate worktree is explicitly requested.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.24.5
notes:
This update polishes the native AppKit conversation interface across turn rendering, scrolling, tool previews, the composer, and task chrome.

## Improved

- Render image attachment strips on user prompts (`PromptAttachmentStripView`, 96 pt expanded / 48 pt folded, up to four thumbnails plus a `+N` overflow badge) with click-to-Quick-Look preview, and add 16 pt horizontal overflow fades and 1.5 s `"Copied"` feedback to `CodeBlockView`.
- Add a floating `ScrollToBottomButton` pill (`Jump to latest`) with a running-turn indicator in `ConversationScrollView`, and support `"Copy Turn as Markdown"` from `StickyToolBar` and `"Open in Terminal"` on command `ToolRowView` rows.
- Animate `FieldPlate` focus, disabled, and image-drag target borders in `ComposerView`, add horizontal wheel scrolling to `AttachmentStripView`, and add a scroll-position thumb indicator to overflowing `CompletionListView` popovers.
- Focus the first invalid control and announce validation errors in `ElicitationCardView`, clear validation errors immediately on edit, tick live expiration countdowns every second, and preserve in-progress elicitation cards across queue count and fence updates in `TaskTailView`.
- Add horizontal overflow edge-fade masks and vertical wheel passthrough to `SessionConfigurationPanel`, semantic status colors and appearance-aware symbol attachments to `ConfigOptionMenuView`, SF Symbol disclosure chevrons and dynamic row heights to `ChiefWorkbenchView`, and consistent hover/pointing-hand states across task chrome controls.

## Fixed

- Fix `TopEdgeFade` limit updates, flipped clip-view mask polarity, and `contentInsets.top` accounting, and skip `ComposerScrollView` and nested scroll views when attaching column fades in `ColumnContainerView`.
- Fix `RollingThoughtPreviewView` flipped coordinates and theme colors, `RollingSubtaskPreviewView` narrow-width truncation and trailing commas, `RollingToolPreviewView` timer cleanup and 1 Hz relayout, and stationary `.began` (`deltaY == 0`) trackpad gesture handoff in `RollingToolWheelRouter`.
- Retain `SummaryBarView` usage tooltip strings across AppKit tooltip registration, remove the 8 pt empty-chip indent, preserve `ToolPartView` text selection across async syntax highlighting, and cancel stale highlight tasks on `ToolRowView` reuse.
- Filter non-image Finder file icons out of `ComposerPasteboard.pictures()`, guard ghost text against the macOS Accent Picker and IME mark transitions, align multi-line `QueuedMessageRow` text to the top line, and clamp narrow status labels.
- Keep `PinnedWorkView` ticking until retained finished items expire even after all running items complete, forward `translucent` and workspace `folder` into `PinnedSubagentExpansionView`, and scope `PermissionCardView` key equivalents so they never intercept IME, terminal, button, or active non-empty composer input.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.24.4
notes:
This update fixes macOS native UI appearance, layout, focus, and interaction issues across the shell, settings, browser, terminal drawer, composer, conversation, and widgets.

## Fixed

- Fix flipped-coordinate hit testing and effective divider rects on `ShellSplitView` so the title bar stays draggable and the bottom inset responds to divider drags and double-clicks.
- Refresh layer colors across `BrowserWorkspaceView`, `BrowserSidebarView`, `BrowserPopovers`, `UpdatePanelView`, `DialogLayerView`, and `DialogSurfaces` when switching between Light, Dark, and Increased Contrast appearances.
- Fix `BrowserTabPillView` hidden media-dot spacing and pinned-tab constraint conflicts, update loading progress width on resize, focus the new-tab search field when opening a new tab, and refresh the sidebar when history or download preferences change.
- Drop hidden Neovim grid focus when filling the terminal drawer (`EditorWorkspaceView.layoutFilled()`), vertically center terminal drawer branch metadata, prevent header label collisions, and keep selected tab underlines inside bounds.
- Add mouse/trackpad wheel scrolling and accessibility frame updates to `CompletionListView`, vertically center short `QueuedMessageRow` items, and tint the missing-attachment fallback icon cleanly in Dark mode.
- Fix `ProviderEditorCard` secondary keyboard navigation (`SettingsSecondaryControls`) and embedded scroll layout, resolve the `RemotePage` add-flow push/pop race, and preserve the settings breadcrumb font size.
- Fix `RollingSubtaskPreviewView` icon/title overlap, `ToolRowView` hover-action chevron occlusion, rounded inline-code styling in expanded `ThoughtScrollView`, and dynamic screenshot/action-button sizing in Widgets.
- Standardize button tinting, selection washes, typography tiers, and corner radii on `AtriumColor`, `AtriumType`, and `AtriumShape`.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.24.2
notes:
Independent work now runs concurrently across model discovery, history loading, read-only agent tools, and task cleanup.

## Improved

- Discover models from up to four providers at a time while preserving configuration order and credential redaction.
- Run adjacent read, list, glob, and grep calls concurrently. Writes, commands, and other stateful tools still wait for earlier reads, and tool results remain in model order. Cancellation closes unfinished calls so the next turn can continue safely.
- Load and parse independent history logs concurrently, while publishing complete refreshes in order. Git branch lookup and memory loading also overlap during agent startup.
- Stop workers, close dedicated browsers and Neovim instances, and interrupt or restart separate terminals concurrently. Each instance still completes its own ordered cleanup; worker logs drain before the batch history refresh.
- Download the update package and checksum together, and cancel remaining downloads when one fails. Prepare independent build dependencies in parallel.
- Allow up to thirty minutes per release-upload attempt, retaining bounded retries for slow connections.

## Validation and limits

Normal and strict cooperative-pool test runs both passed across seven Swift test targets, reporting 3,077 tests with four existing opt-in tests skipped. The 67 Python tests also passed. Event-gated regressions cover overlap, concurrency limits, result order, write barriers, cancellation, and cleanup.

Concurrency is bounded to control resource usage. Real-workload speedups have not been benchmarked; operations sharing protocol, file-write, or UI state retain their required ordering.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.24.1
notes:
Tool-use previews resume following new content after scrolling stops.

## Fixed

- Fixed a rolling preview that could remain stuck after reading earlier tool output. Delayed scroll notifications and layout changes no longer disable following after its resume timer has ended.
- Keep the automatic resume timer active while native scroll events arrive. Reading back still pauses the preview for three seconds; leaving the preview or scrolling to the bottom resumes following immediately.
- Clear a temporary scroll pause when a preview is removed, so showing it again follows the newest content.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.24.0
notes:
Atrium now has a **Browser** workspace alongside Tasks and Terminal, with persistent tabs, website storage, bookmarks, history, and downloads. It uses the system WebKit engine and keeps personal browsing separate from task browser automation.

## Added

- Switch between Tasks, Terminal, and Browser without reloading open pages or losing terminal state. Browser views are created only when needed; restored background tabs load when selected.
- Manage multiple tabs, pin tabs, reopen recently closed tabs, search from the address bar, find text on a page, and adjust zoom.
- Keep cookies and website storage across tabs and restarts in a dedicated profile. Personal browsing data is not exposed through Atrium's task browser tools.
- Browse bookmarks, history, and downloads in the sidebar. Export bookmarks as Netscape HTML, search and delete history entries, and download files with non-overwriting names.
- Show explicit navigation and TLS errors, site permission controls, and recovery notices. Fix a recovery-banner layout crash that could prevent Browser from opening after a restart.

## Fixed

- Fixed a crash when closing an embedded Neovim editor while a background request was still being sent. Shutdown now rejects new requests and synchronizes input-pipe closure with writes.

## Validation and known limits

- Release-app checks covered workspace switching, page form preservation, persistent cookies and local storage, lazy restoration of 20 tabs, downloads and quarantine attributes, history search and deletion, bookmark export, and light/dark layouts. Public HTTPS pages loaded successfully; this does not establish every site's compatibility.
- File upload and bookmark import have not completed end-to-end acceptance: the automated file selection did not succeed, and the cause is undetermined. Full-screen entry/exit checks did not pass.
- Actual media playback, DRM streaming, password/Passkey integration, web notifications, and live WebContent crash recovery remain unverified.
- Some OAuth/SSO providers reject embedded WebKit sign-in. Use Open in System Browser where needed; browser sessions are not transferred between applications.
- Closing a tab may discard an unsaved web form without the same beforeunload confirmation as Safari. Chrome extensions are not supported.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.23.6
notes:
Chief agents can now notice when a worker becomes idle, needs input, or may have stopped making progress. Worker reports remain available until their delivery is confirmed.

## Fixed

- Report worker turn endings, input and permission requests, failures, stops, and sign-in requirements. An idle worker means its current turn has ended; the chief still needs to check whether the assignment is complete.
- Deliver reports to a running chief through the adapter's supported steering mechanism. Unsupported, rejected, or unconfirmed delivery keeps the report pending. Waking an idle chief still requires **Continue after worker reports** to be enabled.
- Check workers every 15 seconds without asking their models to generate heartbeats. After 180 seconds without new agent text, tool progress, or a plan change, report that the worker may be stalled. Waiting for a person's answer is excluded, and unchanged status is not repeated.
- Keep reports through failed delivery and history restoration. A late acknowledgement cannot remove a newer report. Respect stopped tasks and cancelled queued reports, and remove input or permission reminders once they have been answered.
- Ask workers to give concise updates at meaningful milestones and explain remaining work before ending a turn. Task listings also expose pending reports, input requests, and known idle duration.

## Validation and limits

Automated coverage includes injected-clock monitoring and real local daemon/ACP connections to controlled test agents, including delivery failures, late acknowledgements, cancellation, restoration, and resolved input requests. Live model and adapter combinations have not all been tested; delivery to a running chief depends on the adapter's steering and acknowledgement support.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.23.5
notes:
All top-level ACP agents can direct workers when **Tasks can create workers** is enabled, including the built-in Atrium agent. Tool-call previews show syntax colors again.

## Fixed

- Removed the hidden per-agent `canDirect` setting. Old saved values no longer prevent an agent from receiving task dispatch tools; worker model choices remain unchanged.
- Connected the built-in Atrium agent to the same task-scoped worker tools used by external agents, including creating, waiting for, reading and closing workers. Worker ownership, model rules, fence inheritance and the restriction against workers creating more workers remain enforced.
- Restored syntax highlighting for shell commands and source code in the rolling tool preview. Highlighting handles Unicode text, appearance and font changes, and reused preview rows, while keeping parsing bounded to the visible output.

## Updating

Reopen a task after updating to receive its dispatch tools. Existing live agent processes do not gain tools automatically.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.23.4
notes:
Terminal tab switching avoids redundant configuration and geometry updates, and rendering keeps a short, refresh-rate-independent idle window to reduce display-link churn during rapid output.

## Fixed

- Closing a terminal can finish even if its relay ignores the normal shutdown signal. Relays also preserve the caller's working directory and environment without a redundant privileged login process.
- Mixed light and dark windows retain their terminal colors after app appearance or font settings change.
- Input method candidate positions update when terminals move between windows or within a layout.
- Reattaching or restoring a terminal filters historical device, cursor, mode and color queries so their replies do not appear as shell input. Queries from a still-running program, shell startup and live output remain available to the newly attached terminal.
- Reused terminal tabs keep the correct title, error state and select/close targets after replacement or reordering.
- The first click on **Dismiss** now works when leaving the task list: focus changes preserve the pressed error-card button until mouse-up. Permission hints update without replacing their card.

The renderer retains VSync, font rendering, ligatures and window translucency/blur. Its CoreVideo start/stop operations remain on the main thread, and its idle deadline is safe across synchronous and renderer-thread draws.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.23.0
notes:
Antigravity and Codex sessions now support more of their native workflows, including interactive questions, selective session import and recovery after an agent exits.

## Added

- Antigravity tasks can append instructions when creating a session and display the subscription tier reported by the agent.
- Codex supports mid-turn steering through its native steering request, interactive forms and sign-in links, and native conversation forks when the adapter offers them.
- New Task can list an agent's external sessions and import a selected conversation. Import preserves the selected permission mode and rebuilds history from supported replay APIs. Failed imports show an error and retain the selected session for retry.
- Interactive forms support choices, text, numbers, checkboxes and multiple selections, with validation before submission. Each question's choices remain independent.
- Failed sessions can reconnect in place. Reauthentication preserves the original native conversation; an interrupted prompt is restored as a draft instead of being sent again automatically. Related tasks inherit the parent's permission settings and compatible configuration preferences.

## Fixed

- Antigravity context usage follows the agent's reported context window instead of cumulative billing tokens. Empty late usage updates no longer erase established usage.
- Agent request cancellation and completed questions dismiss pending interactions without sending duplicate responses.
- Temporary worktree paths display consistently in the editor and touched-file list.

## Known issues

- The global terminal and Scratch Terminal window still share a render surface; one can appear blank when the other refreshes.
- After a task follows a new worktree, its terminal's + button uses the existing terminal's directory. Command-T uses the task's directory in the Tasks workspace.
- Opening a task from a notification or the menu bar does not automatically switch from Terminal to Tasks.
- The task terminal's Control-` shortcut remains enabled in the global terminal workspace and can redirect keyboard focus to the hidden task terminal.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.
- Session listing, native forks and replay depend on the capabilities advertised by the installed agent adapter.

title: Atrium 0.22.0
notes:
The main window now switches between Tasks and a global terminal workspace.

## Added

- A Tasks / Terminal switch in the toolbar opens a terminal workspace without selecting a task. The toolbar shows the number of global terminal tabs.
- The global terminal supports multiple tabs, with new tabs starting in the selected terminal's current directory. Command-T creates a global terminal tab while this workspace is selected.
- New Task and Next Blocked Task return to the task workspace. The task selection is preserved when switching between Tasks and Terminal.

## Known issues

- The global terminal and the existing Scratch Terminal window share a render surface. Using both can leave one blank when the other refreshes, including while hidden.
- After a task follows a new worktree, its terminal's + button starts a tab in the existing terminal's directory instead of the task's updated directory. Command-T still uses the task's directory in the Tasks workspace.
- Opening a task from a notification or the menu bar does not switch back from Terminal to Tasks automatically.
- The task terminal's Control-` shortcut remains enabled in the global terminal workspace. It can change the hidden task drawer and redirect keyboard focus to that task's terminal.

## Requirements

- Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27 or later.

title: Atrium 0.21.0
notes:
Agents can now manage their own worktrees, use a dedicated browser, and control local Mac apps. The Web client adds files, diffs, history, and terminals.

## Added

- Chief tasks can create and inspect managed worktrees, collect worker reports, and send selected reports back to the chief. Automatic continuation is available as an explicit task setting and remains off by default. Worktree removal refuses active or dirty workspaces.
- The Web client can browse workspace files, display text and binary diffs, and load older task history in pages. Its terminal supports desktop and phone layouts, Unicode input, resizing, reconnecting to the same shell, and explicit close. Logging out revokes active terminal connections.
- Each task can use a dedicated Chrome/Chromium profile through browser tools. Actions leave screenshots in the conversation and the latest image in the inspector. Task settings can disable the browser or enable page scripts, which are off by default. Closing the task closes its browser.
- Local unfenced tasks can observe and operate running Mac apps through desktop tools. Operations show a visible control banner; external input pauses control, and only the person can resume it in task settings. Password fields refuse text and key input. Desktop control is serialized because the desktop is shared between tasks.
- Browser and desktop screenshots can reach the native agent's model providers as images, while remaining visible in the task's history.

## Fixed

- Desktop helpers no longer take foreground focus while starting. Their own clicks and keys no longer trigger a false user-takeover pause on the next step, and a stop shortcut received by the active monitor is intercepted before reaching the target app.
- Direct remote terminal streams handle framed input, output, resize, and exit messages consistently.
- Release asset uploads have bounded retries in both repositories, and isolated app checks clean up their own system preference domains and provide an opaque backdrop for transparent-window screenshots.

## Requirements

- The release package is for Apple silicon Macs running macOS 27 or later.
- Browser tools require an installed Chrome or Chromium. They use task-owned profiles, not the person's existing browser session.
- Desktop tools require Accessibility, Screen Recording, and Input Monitoring permission, checked from Atrium Settings. They are local-only and available only to unfenced tasks. User-browser takeover, remote desktop control, and live screen streaming are outside this release.

title: Atrium 0.20.0
notes:
The timeline now shows which work is still apart from the main line, and where it came from.

## Changed

- Only live tasks in their own worktree or started from a visible parent have a branch. Folder tasks and finished tasks sit on the trunk. A related task leaves its parent's row; nested workers and sub-agents connect downward from that row.
- Hover a task or its branch's origin to keep its ancestors and descendants visible while unrelated tasks dim. Click an origin to select the parent, or use the row's “Show Origin” accessibility action.
- The timeline's context menu offers continuation, review and handoff using the same availability rules as the task pane. Handoff is also available in the task pane's More menu and opens a card with another agent selected.
- A newly arriving branch grows from its origin. When a task ends, its line fades and its node moves to the trunk; its children immediately connect to the parent's new position. Layout, selection and accessibility are ready throughout the animation.

- Workspace dividers now align to backing pixels on 1× displays, keeping the task controls and terminal drawer flush during transitions.

## Validation

- Full normal and strict cooperative-pool suites: 2,877 tests each; four existing opt-in IME/large-tree checks remain skipped.
- Isolated Release windows: timeline forks in dark/light at motion scales 0 and 10, typography, shell, chief, editor, and selection latency. All measured latency targets remain within their limits.
- Python release/tooling tests: 50; harness tests: 41.

title: Atrium 0.19.0
notes:
The AppKit window now moves as one: opening a drawer or changing the controls makes room without losing the conversation's bottom, and opening a tool shows where the rows below it went.

## Changed

- Task selection fades the new task in; holding an arrow key keeps intermediate selections immediate. Tool groups, thoughts, tool output and subtask details move the rows below them as they open or close.
- Terminal drawers, session settings, pinned work and the widget column now have arrival and departure transitions. Review controls and queued messages move with the conversation's bottom edge. Reversing a transition continues from what is on screen.
- Motion uses four durations: 120 ms to leave, 150 ms to change, 200 ms to enter, and 300 ms to make room. Layout, input and accessibility reach their final state immediately; streaming updates remain immediate.
- Dragged column dividers settle on a grid and catch their default widths. Double-clicking either divider restores its width. The timeline and widget column settle at a nearby row when a trackpad scroll ends.

## Fixed

- Cancelling the first of several queued messages fades that message, preserving the rows for the messages still waiting. A first prompt sent while an agent starts says that it is waiting for the agent to start.
- Opening a fold or pinned work reveals its content as the rows below make room, so text does not overlap during the transition. Accessibility actions can expand and collapse long thoughts without losing the action response.
- A conversation following its bottom stays there when the controls change height; a conversation scrolled back keeps the row being read in place. The composer's text now sits inside the padding its measurement reserves.
- Upgrading from the previous window implementation preserves the saved window position and size. New windows use the display in use for their initial placement.
- Long automatic titles end with an ellipsis, emphasis markers do not leak into thought previews, and a failed turn shows its error once on its card.

## How it was checked

- The complete Swift suite passed in normal and strict cooperative-pool modes: 2,857 tests in each run.
- Four existing opt-in tests remained skipped: two require real input-method focus, and two are large-tree benchmarks.
- Motion tests inspect the actual layer animations, sample a frozen Core Animation clock, compare scale 0 and animated end states, reverse transitions in flight, and check conversation measurement counts and bottom-following geometry.
- The Release app ran 31 motion scenarios in dark and light appearances at scales 0 and 10. Both appearances ended with the same selected task and view geometry; slow-motion screenshots were checked for clipping, overlaps and bottom alignment.

## Motion exception

When a narrow window needs more width to show widgets, its outer frame changes immediately. The widget column still animates in. Animating the window frame would reflow text on every frame and delay the final input geometry.
